stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google has launched Gemini 4 Carbon, positioning it as a major advancement in frontier AI models.
The new model claims significant improvements in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity capabilities.
Gemini 4 Carbon reportedly leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark against competitors like Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra.

stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware affects most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: arstechnica.com via aCaB
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware.
The vulnerability affects a vast majority of servers globally, indicating widespread risk.
This represents a significant, high-severity security vulnerability impacting core server infrastructure.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta's Llama 3 8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags including 'transformers' and 'text-generation'.
The content serves as a benchmark indicator for the performance and popularity of the Llama architecture.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for autonomous agents.
The model is designed for persistent, multi-step tasks, context gathering, and tool calling on local hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google attributes year-over-year growth in search queries to its investments in Artificial Intelligence.
CEO Sundar Pichai stated that AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries.
The company reported that its query growth rate is the highest among its peers in the Q3 2026 earnings.

stories.title: Amazon turns its most capable smart speaker into a smart camera, too
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: Amazon is integrating camera capabilities into its Echo Studio smart speaker.
The new 'Echo Studio with Home Camera' allows the device to 'see and understand' its surroundings.
This represents an expansion of smart speaker functionality into visual monitoring and AI-driven scene understanding.

stories.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
stories.author: Fu-En Yang
bullet_points: Introduces ThinkWorld, a new VLA learning framework designed to improve robotic manipulation.
Addresses the generalization limitations of current VLA models by leveraging human videos for broader experience.
Overcomes the data scaling vs. action grounding trade-off by grounding action reasoning in world dynamics.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel prompt injection defense mechanism.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation in LLMs.
Evaluated on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and GPT-OSS-20B, showing promise against state-of-the-art defenses.

stories.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
stories.author: Alexander Toshev
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of building high-performing LLM agents capable of complex, multi-step task completion using tools.
A novel pipeline, SynthAPI, is proposed to systematically control the diversity of synthetically generated tool-use environments.
The study investigates how varying environmental composition (tools, tasks, databases) impacts the training efficacy of these tool-using agents.

stories.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
stories.author: Yves-Alexandre de Montjoye
bullet_points: Introduces 'Heads of Security' (HoS), a novel defense mechanism against prompt injection attacks.
HoS uses learned per-head attention gates to enforce instruction-data separation within LLMs.
Evaluated on large models like Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, showing potential against state-of-the-art defenses.

stories.title: Metacognitive Decoding: Efficient Inference for Diffusion Language Agents
stories.author: Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullet_points: Introduces a 'metacognitive controller' to guide diffusion language model generation.
The controller optimizes computational efficiency by determining when to finalize tokens and generation length.
Aims to improve the efficiency of diffusion language agents during interaction with an environment.

stories.title: Follow the Gradient: Tracing Safety Degradation Back to Training Data
stories.author: Pratyush Maini
bullet_points: Fine-tuning LLMs on seemingly benign instruction data can silently degrade their safety.
Standard content filters are ineffective because the safety-degrading data appears harmless.
The paper introduces SimpleLoRIF, a gradient embedding method to trace safety degradation back to specific fine-tuning examples.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial integration features Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech in five languages.
The system demonstrates high performance, streaming audio over 100x faster than real-time on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection has released its first open-weight model, Beam, available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for software engineering, reasoning, and complex agentic tasks.
The model is currently offered for free access via Ollama's cloud for a limited duration.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses deployment and security concerns for running local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
Decision models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges the gap between proprietary AI services (Claude) and local, open-source LLMs (via Ollama).

stories.title: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Akai is adopting an open-source approach for its upcoming MPC Sample Key.
The company is actively engaging with the modding and custom firmware development community.
This move signals a shift toward greater user customization and hacker enablement in music hardware.

stories.title: Readwise is taking on Kindle and Kobo for ebook supremacy
stories.author: David Pierce
bullet_points: Readwise is expanding its ecosystem with the launch of Readwise Books.
The new offering aims to compete directly with established ebook platforms like Kindle and Kobo.
Readwise targets 'power readers' by integrating highlight management across various content types (Kindle, newsletters, PDFs).

stories.title: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft reported strong Q1 2027 financial results, achieving $92.3 billion in revenue.
The company demonstrated significant growth, with revenue up 19% and net income increasing by 32%.
Microsoft is undergoing a financial reporting overhaul as part of its new fiscal year structure.

stories.title: Foreign gadget bans: all the news about the FCC’s clampdown on Chinese tech
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: The US government is implementing restrictions on the import of certain Chinese consumer electronics.
The crackdown targets various gadgets, including drones, routers, and Roombas.
The policy is framed as a response to national security concerns, though the article suggests xenophobic undertones.

stories.title: Microsoft is ending Copilot support on smart TVs
stories.author: Andrew Liszewski
bullet_points: Microsoft is discontinuing Copilot support on smart TVs this year.
The removal follows previous announcements from LG and Samsung regarding Copilot integration.
The news is currently based on a report from Windows Central rather than an official company statement.

stories.title: The last, best hope for space tourism just rolled onto a runway in Arizona
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: The article discusses a recent development in the space tourism sector.
The new development is positioned as a potential breakthrough or 'last, best hope' for the industry.
The context notes a recent lull in space tourism flights.

stories.title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Google's AI exhibits bias or caution when responding to questions about the 2020 US election.
The AI's responses become more direct or less guarded when the query is directed outside the United States.
The story highlights ongoing concerns regarding the political neutrality and guardrails implemented in large language models.

stories.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Apple has introduced a new MacBook Pro featuring an OLED touchscreen display.
The OLED display technology is highlighted as the primary selling point of the new model.
The high cost of the new MacBook Pro is noted as a significant consideration for potential buyers.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' novel planar hexagonal surface elements designed for efficient 3D scene and 2D image representation.
Addresses the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis techniques like radiance fields and splatting.
Hexels leverage locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance to reduce the number of required primitives.

stories.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
stories.author: Zhi-Song Liu
bullet_points: KPPax bridges the gap between traditional atmospheric chemistry modeling (KPP language) and modern machine learning frameworks.
It converts kinetic mechanisms into differentiable, just-in-time compiled, and vectorizable code using JAX.
The tool enables the integration of complex atmospheric chemistry simulations directly into differentiable programming pipelines for ML applications.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: The research explores whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can autonomously discover hidden or altered physical laws.
A framework named LongChang is introduced to simulate environments with modified physical laws for testing.
The core hypothesis is that LLMs might identify unexpected physical behaviors (e.g., altered gravity) without explicit guidance.

stories.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
stories.author: Mingyi Hong
bullet_points: The research introduces MuonGS, a method for pretraining Large Language Models (LLMs) using relaxed weight-norm control.
The study investigates the role of weight decay and explicit weight-norm constraints in improving optimizer performance during LLM pretraining.
A novel metric, the 'accumulated effective learning rate' ($C_T$), is used to analyze norm control across the entire training trajectory.

stories.title: What Improves During Pretraining? Tracking Knowledge Acquisition with Point-in-Time Models
stories.author: Yao Lu
bullet_points: The research investigates how language models acquire general versus domain-specific knowledge during pretraining.
Point-in-time models, trained on web snapshots from different years, are used to track knowledge evolution over time.
A new metric, the Temporal Variability Score (TVS), is proposed to quantify how knowledge prevalence changes across time.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of how Large Language Model (LLM) group discussions are summarized into a concise memory for a final decision-maker.
It investigates two natural heuristics for memory compression: retaining the rarest claims or retaining claims relevant to the decision criteria.
The authors introduce 'CrossProfile,' a new diagnostic benchmark designed to test these memory and decision-making capabilities in LLMs.

stories.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
stories.author: Shilei Wen
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) where language-based reasoning causes 'visual forgetting' when processing video.
Existing methods for maintaining visual grounding are limited, often relying on textual coordinates to specify symbolic locations.
VideoLVR proposes a new approach to enable models to reliably revisit relevant visual evidence during complex video reasoning.

stories.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
stories.author: Alan Yuille
bullet_points: Introduces 'Hexels,' a novel planar hexagonal surface element designed for efficient 3D scene representation.
Aims to address the high memory and computational demands of modern view synthesis and 3D reconstruction techniques (like radiance fields and splatting).
Hexels leverage locally planar regions with smoothly varying appearance to use fewer, larger primitives for better efficiency.

stories.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
stories.author: Yu Chen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the instability of test-time adaptation (TTA), where interventions can help one batch but harm subsequent ones.
The authors propose PORTAL, a controller designed to intelligently decide when and how to apply model interventions.
The research highlights the limitation of average accuracy metrics and suggests using target labels to guide intervention decisions.

stories.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
stories.author: Claire Tomlin
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of limited dexterity in robotic manipulation, focusing on in-hand object pose reaching.
Highlights the critical but often unmeasured aspect of safety during complex in-hand maneuvers.
Presents research pushing the boundaries of learned hand skills for diverse and difficult grasping tasks.

stories.title: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Wentao Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the computational expense of generating and verifying rollouts in large-scale language agent environments.
Introduces EnvSched, a system designed for environment-aware scheduling in agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Aims to improve RL efficiency by organizing, evaluating, and scheduling task instances alongside their defining environments.

stories.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
stories.author: Rui Wu
bullet_points: Introduces GAS-PFN, a new model for zero-shot traffic forecasting that handles complex spatiotemporal dynamics.
Addresses the limitation of traditional graph-based models which require retraining for new road networks.
Utilizes Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) to enable in-context inference using synthetic task priors for domain adaptation.

stories.title: Understanding the limits of latent world models
stories.author: Steffen Schneider
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current world model evaluations, which often focus only on task performance.
It introduces the concept of 'faithful latent world models' to assess the quality of learned dynamics.
Faithfulness is defined using an equivariance condition between the environment's transition map and the learned latent dynamics.

stories.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
stories.author: Amir Gholami
bullet_points: Addresses limitations in current LLM agent learning (e.g., GEPA) where failures might not yield useful signals.
Proposes 'GEPA-Curator' to curate tasks provided to self-improving agents, mitigating harmful or noisy learning data.
Focuses on improving robustness in complex, multi-turn agentic workloads by addressing prompt weaknesses and execution noise.

stories.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
stories.author: Ying-Cong Chen
bullet_points: The research explores whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can autonomously discover hidden or altered physical laws.
A framework named LongChang is introduced to simulate environments with modified physical laws for testing.
The core question is whether LLMs can detect unexpected physical behaviors without explicit guidance on what to investigate.

stories.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
stories.author: Zhiwei Deng
bullet_points: The paper addresses the quadratic time complexity bottleneck of self-attention in long-sequence LLMs.
It introduces 'Multi-State Linear Attention' (MSLA) to improve efficiency by segmenting and compressing context.
The proposed method uses mean alignment between queries and segment keys for information aggregation.

stories.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
stories.author: Khalil El Khammar
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical issue in LLM group decision-making: how to effectively compress complex discussions into a short memory for a final decision-maker.
It investigates two heuristics for memory compression—retaining the rarest claims or claims relevant to decision criteria—and notes their ambiguity in hidden-profile tasks.
The authors introduce 'CrossProfile,' a new diagnostic benchmark featuring 60 templates to test the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant information in LLM group settings.

stories.title: Teach reality, not ethics: a drop-in continued-pretraining corpus installs coupled human-biosphere-AI welfare dispositions across model families
stories.author: Mingxun Wang
bullet_points: Addresses a critical gap in LLM training: the lack of ecological reasoning regarding living systems.
Introduces a novel 'coupled welfare' corpus designed to train models on human-biosphere-AI dependencies and irreversible harm.
Aims to mitigate the risk of LLMs making decisions that could irreversibly destroy living systems when deployed operationally.

stories.title: The Grid, a factory-scale robot in Massachusetts that builds PCBs on demand
stories.author: seddona
bullet_points: Introduction of 'The Grid,' a factory-scale robotic system.
The system is designed to build Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) on demand.
The technology is based in Massachusetts, suggesting industrial automation advancements.

stories.title: Apple's git still trusts the compromised eMudhra certificates
stories.author: emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com by galadran
bullet_points: The article reports a security vulnerability where Apple's Git system continues to trust compromised eMudhra certificates.
This indicates a potential weakness in Apple's certificate trust mechanisms or dependency handling.
The issue is a specific security flaw related to certificate validation, impacting developers or users relying on Apple's Git infrastructure.

stories.title: Your Laptop Might Replace Most of Your AI Bill
stories.author: carlastabile
bullet_points: The article discusses the potential for local, on-device AI processing to reduce reliance on cloud computing costs.
It addresses the common assumption that high-quality AI requires expensive cloud infrastructure.
The content suggests that modern laptop hardware may now be capable of running substantial AI models locally.

stories.title: How to cut your AI agent's input tokens: what worked, what failed, and a bench to measure yours
stories.author: anis_meziani_52aab42304a8
bullet_points: Addresses the critical operational cost issue of large AI agent token consumption.
Provides practical, field-tested strategies and a 7-point checklist for token reduction.
Offers an open-source benchmark for developers to measure their own agent efficiency.
